title: Tool Calling & Function Invocation in .NET
description: Master function calling in .NET using AIFunctionFactory, strongly-typed schemas, parameter validation, and self-correcting error loops.

data.text: How Tool Calling Operates Under the Hood

Tool calling (or function calling) enables LLMs to take structured actions in the external world. Rather than executing code directly inside the model's neural network, the model acts as an intelligent dispatcher: when presented with a list of available tool schemas, it evaluates the user query and generates a structured JSON payload specifying which function to invoke and what argument values to provide. The hosting .NET application executes the actual method in code and feeds the return value back to the model.

data.caption: The Function Calling Execution Roundtrip in .NET
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as React Frontend / User
    participant DotNet as ASP.NET Core Application
    participant Model as LLM (OpenAI / Azure)
    participant DB as SQL Database / API

    User->>DotNet: 'What is the stock level of SKU-104 in Chicago?'
    DotNet->>Model: CompleteAsync(messages, tools: [GetStockLevelSchema])
    Model-->>DotNet: FunctionCall(name: 'GetStockLevel', args: { sku: 'SKU-104', warehouse: 'Chicago' })
    DotNet->>DB: Execute SQL / API query
    DB-->>DotNet: { inStock: 42, reserved: 5 }
    DotNet->>Model: Submit FunctionResultContent({ inStock: 42, reserved: 5 })
    Model-->>DotNet: 'There are currently 42 units of SKU-104 in stock in Chicago (5 reserved).'
    DotNet-->>User: Grounded Answer

data.text: In Microsoft.Extensions.AI, you can define tools effortlessly from standard C# methods using AIFunctionFactory.Create. The library automatically generates the underlying JSON Schema—including parameter types, nullability, descriptions, and enum options—via reflection and System.ComponentModel Description attributes.

data.text: When a tool execution throws an exception (for example, due to an invalid SKU format or database connection timeout), never crash the application or return a generic 500 error to the user. Instead, catch the exception and return an informative error message inside the Tool message. Modern LLMs are adept at reading the error feedback, adjusting their input arguments, and retrying the tool call correctly.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tool calling uses the LLM as an intelligent dispatcher while executing verified C# code in the host app
Use AIFunctionFactory.Create with [Description] attributes to automatically derive precise JSON schemas
Include clear semantic descriptions on every parameter to guide the model's argument selection
Return structured validation errors back to the model to empower autonomous self-correction
Never execute unvalidated tool arguments on database queries without parameterized inputs
data.takeaway: Tool calling is the primary mechanism for agentic action. By pairing strongly-typed C# methods with detailed schema descriptions and self-correcting error handling, .NET developers build safe, resilient integrations.
